intro: How the business is doing, read straight from your own books: margins, cash, customers, operations and risk, each number with what it means, what moved it and whether to trust it yet. Nothing here changes your records; it only reads them.
start: Open the Executive summary and choose a period at the top. Each card says what its number means.
Press How this is worked out on a card you rely on, to see the figures it is made of.
Set a target on the numbers that matter to you, so a card says when it needs a look.
Press Customise to keep the cards you read and put the rest away.

articles.title: Find out how a number is worked out
articles.summary: Every card opens to the figures it is made of, taken from your own records, with a link to the records behind each one.

tips: Provisional means something it depends on is not in yet, such as a journal entry waiting to be posted. The reason is written under it.
A forecast is a look ahead, never a fact. The dashed chip says so.

articles.title: Set a target for a number
articles.summary: Say what a number should be at least or at most, and the line to warn from, so its card tells you when it needs a look.

steps.lead: Open How this is worked out
steps.rest: on the card.

steps.lead: Choose At least or At most:
steps.rest: a floor the number should stay above, or a ceiling it should stay below.

steps.lead: Enter the target and Warn from.
steps.rest: Between the two, the card says Needs a look; past the warning line, Needs action.
The card shows how far it is from the target today.

tips: Only people who manage the alerts of that part of the business can set a target.
Back to the default removes your target.

articles.title: Choose which cards a dashboard shows
articles.summary: Switch cards on and off, drag them into order and size them. Your arrangement is yours; others keep theirs.

steps.rest: at the top of the dashboard.

steps.lead: Switch a card on to add it,
steps.rest: or off to put it away. Only numbers you may read are listed, and nothing is deleted.

steps.lead: Drag a card, or use its arrows,
steps.rest: to change the order. The size chip sets how wide it is.
The page becomes your own arrangement. Back to the default gives you the standard page again.

tips: If you may change roles, open Defaults for a role, choose the role and press Set as the role default. People who arranged their own keep theirs.

articles.summary: Cash today, three versions of the next 90 days, and the first day any of them falls below the cash you want to keep.

articles.title: See what it costs to win a customer
articles.summary: Customers won, spend and cost per customer by channel, and whether they come back, month by month.

steps.rest: Customers by channel shows new customers, spend and cost per customer for each channel.
It comes from the books first: the bills and expense claims tagged to your campaigns.

tips: Spend you record by hand counts toward the channel's cost per customer. It does not change the books.
